item.description: The Bus is celebrating fifty years of service in the Rutland region. Marble Valley Regional Transit District runs nearly fifty vehicles across ten routes, partnering with local businesses and healthcare providers. They’re planning upgrades including hybrid buses and new rider support programs.

Port Henry in Essex County, New York, has a new 'Champ' sightings board. It replaces a board that stood for over forty years and lists more than one hundred thirty reported sightings of the legendary Lake Champlain creature. The town used occupancy tax funds to commission and install the colorful new sign.

Rutland is updating the way it replaces police cruisers, now factoring in idling time as part of mileage wear. One hour of idling equals thirty miles of driving, officials say. The policy change awaits final approval by the city and state.

A Poultney man has been convicted of multiple sexual assault charges involving a child. William Rice Jr. faces life in prison for his crimes, a Rutland County court ruled. Sentencing will be determined in the coming months.
